edge_semantics: Each route all_of is AND. Routes in alternative_group D3-sufficient-routes are OR. Printed-source and derived-application layers are distinct. Inputs are source obligations, not assertions of Lean implementation dependencies.

printed_and_gap_nodes.content: Opening game and its three bullets: rounds t=1,...,T; adversary chooses y_t in [0,1] secretly; player chooses x_t in [0,1]; observation follows the prediction; loss is (x_t-y_t)^2. This is the information-order source.
Paragraph beginning “Let's start”: common fixed distribution on [0,1], independent identically distributed draws, distribution selected at the beginning and unknown to learner.

Same paragraph's claims: predicting the distribution mean each round gives expected total sigma^2 T and no admissible strategy does better. An explicit causal/measurable randomized policy model and the proof of this assertion are not printed.
Equation (1.1): E_{Y_1,...,Y_T}[sum_{t=1}^T (x_t-Y_t)^2] - sigma^2 T. It is an expected centered total; the source's expectation subscript does not include an explicit auxiliary seed.
Equation (1.2): (1/T) E[sum_{t=1}^T (x_t-Y_t)^2] - sigma^2. Positive integer horizons are implicit.
Paragraph after (1.2), first assertion: both quantities are nonnegative. Depends on admissible information, not bounded outputs alone. The proof is omitted.

Remaining paragraph: success means the quantity in (1.1) grows sublinearly, equivalently (1.2) tends to zero. This is an equivalence of criteria, not a theorem asserting that every learner succeeds. Variance is the difficulty normalization.

Opening rewrite display: E[sum (x_t-Y_t)^2] - min_{x in [0,1]} E[sum (x-Y_t)^2]. The minimum is OUTSIDE expectation. The fixed oracle comparator is a constant chosen to minimize expected cumulative loss.

Next paragraph and displayed Regret_T: remove distribution assumptions and use arbitrary deterministic observations; for a deterministic algorithm define sum (x_t-y_t)^2 - min_x sum (x-y_t)^2 and require sublinear growth. Here minimum is pathwise, unlike P02-FIXED.
Paragraph beginning “Note that”: fixed single best predictor versus comparator sequences; keeps fixed comparator as the present benchmark.

Generalization paragraph and Regret_T(u) display: V subset of R^d, predictions x_t in V, real losses ell_t:V->R, arbitrary fixed u in V, sum ell_t(x_t)-sum ell_t(u). Supplies the setting for Lemma 1.2.

Paragraph after general regret: algorithm need not know u or its regret to guarantee a bound; for every fixed u, no-regret is “at most sublinear,” printed as lim Regret_T(u)/T <= 0. This signed one-sided condition must not be conflated with the zero-limit criterion in P01-SUCCESS.
Remark 1.1: regret also depends on the entire loss sequence; dependence suppressed in notation.

“A Winning Strategy” paragraph: arbitrary data, even an adversary selecting its observation after seeing the learner prediction. This is a deterministic pathwise guarantee, not an independence assumption.
Best-in-hindsight paragraph and display: x*_T = argmin_{x in [0,1]} sum (x-y_t)^2 = (1/T)sum y_t. Existence, feasibility and the minimization identity are asserted, not proved.
Paragraph following display: future optimizer unavailable, use optimum on past; stability of the leader is the proposed mechanism, not a distributional prediction.
Final full paragraph: t>=2 predicts x_t=x*_{t-1}=(1/(t-1))sum_{i=1}^{t-1} y_i; first round may be any [0,1] point in this informal proposal; names Follow-the-Leader. Theorem 1.3 later fixes x_1=1/2.

Lemma 1.2 statement/display: arbitrary real losses on V subset R^d and a minimizer x*_t in argmin_{x in V} sum_{i=1}^t ell_i(x) for every relevant t; sum_t ell_t(x*_t) <= sum_t ell_t(x*_T). No convexity, stochasticity or differentiability is assumed. Existence of each minimizer is an explicit lemma premise.
Induction proof's T=1 displayed reflexive inequality ell_1(x*_1)<=ell_1(x*_1).
T>=2 induction hypothesis and displayed full-horizon goal, before (1.3). These are induction structure, not new public assumptions of the lemma.
Equation (1.3) and its justification: cancel identical last terms; it suffices to compare sums to T-1 evaluated at x*_t versus x*_T.
First display after (1.3): sum_{t<T} ell_t(x*_t)<=sum_{t<T} ell_t(x*_{T-1}), by the induction hypothesis.
Second display after (1.3): sum_{t<T}ell_t(x*_{T-1})<=sum_{t<T}ell_t(x*_T), by prefix minimization and feasibility x*_T in V.
Proof's closing sentence chains P04-APPLYIH and P04-PREFIXMIN to (1.3), restores the canceled term and closes induction.
Paragraph before Theorem 1.3: logarithmic upper bound will be proved; minimax optimality/unavoidable logarithmic dependence is explicitly not proved here.
Theorem 1.3 full statement/display: arbitrary y_1,...,y_T in [0,1], strictly-past empirical mean for t>=2, x_1=x*_0=0.5; hindsight regret <=4+4 ln T. T is a positive integer horizon.
Figure 1.1, caption and the curves 1/x and 1/(x-1): graphical explanation of the harmonic-sum upper bound. It illustrates P06-INTEGRAL and is not an independent alternative proof of the theorem.

Proof's first two-line display: replace the hindsight minimum by loss of x*_T, replace x_t by x*_{t-1}, then use Lemma 1.2 to obtain Regret_T <= sum_t [(x*_{t-1}-y_t)^2-(x*_t-y_t)^2]. The BTL subtraction direction matters.
t=1 paragraph/display: (x*_0-y_1)^2-(x*_1-y_1)^2<=0.5^2, using x*_0=1/2 and x*_1=y_1.
t>=2 display lines 1–3: expand squares, factor (x*_{t-1}+x*_t-2y_t)(x*_{t-1}-x*_t), upper bound by absolute values, then by 2\|x*_{t-1}-x*_t\| using unit-interval feasibility.
Same display's next two lines: substitute both empirical means and rewrite their difference as (1/(t-1)-1/t)sum_{i<t}y_i - y_t/t.
Final line of same display: triangle inequality, 1/(t(t-1)) factor, \|sum_{i<t}y_i\|<=t-1 and \|y_t\|<=1 yield difference of losses <=2/t+2\|y_t\|/t<=4/t.
“Hence, overall” display: Regret_T <=0.25+4 sum_{t=2}^T 1/t <=4 sum_{t=1}^T1/t. Empty tail sum handles T=1.
Last paragraph, continuing on p6: interpret harmonic sum as gray area and compare with a shifted reciprocal integral plus the first term.
Top continuation and display: sum_{t=1}^T1/t <=1+integral_2^{T+1}1/(t-1) dt =1+ln T. The T=1 integral is zero.
“Putting everything together” closes Theorem 1.3 using P05-SUM and P06-INTEGRAL.
Proof-summary paragraph: BTL compares with leader sequence and successive leaders differ at rate 1/t, explaining sublinear regret. It restates the proved route, not a second sufficient route.
P03-MINIMIZER and P05-BTL use the finite-sample squared-loss minimization identity without proof. Needed expansion: sum_i(x-y_i)^2=sum_i(m-y_i)^2+T(x-m)^2, m in [0,1].
P01-ORACLE and P02-FIXED omit the mean/variance expansion and proof of the expected fixed-comparator minimum. Marginal same-law boundedness suffices for this part.

P01-ORACLE and P01-NONNEG omit a formal causal-information/independence argument. With IID data and a measurable predictor based on past observations and independent internal randomness, expected squared loss = variance + expected squared distance of prediction from the mean.
P01-SUCCESS states an equivalence without formal asymptotic derivation: centered average equals centered total divided by positive T; signed total is o(T) iff that quotient tends to zero.
